chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: Singers who play piano: Carmen McRae, Sarah, Dinah Washington and Nat King Cole
summary: They discuss which singers accompany themselves and how Nat Cole moved from trio leader to standing singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah. All these girls, like Sarah, Ella,
Carmen MacRae, she plays, Dinah Washington played very well.
Did you work with Dinah too?
No, I never worked with her. And -- well, she didn't need me because she had some good people behind her.
Yeah.
You know, very good.
I know Sarah doesn't like to play for herself, because I was over at a party at Carmen's house, and Carmen sat down and played and sang, and --
Yeah.
-- then Sarah was going to -- see, Carmen asked Sarah to do the same thing.
Yeah.
And Sarah said, 'I can't play while I'm singing. I can't do it.'
No.
And Carmen said, 'Try,' and so Sarah tried and she said, 'I can't do it.' But Benny Carter came in and played the piano for Sarah to sing.
Yeah.
And Carmen said she couldn't understand why Sarah couldn't do it. 'I can play the piano but I can't do it at the same time I'm singing.'
Well, I'll tell you who else I think became that way was Nat King Cole. When he had the trio he
always played behind himself, with the trio. But to stand up to sing, and concentrate as a -- you know --

Well, I think that was part of the image he wanted or Maria wanted him to be a stand up singer, and I think he thought he wasn't as much of a star if he was accompanying himself. I mean wasn't that the approach?
Well, I think you're right about that.
It was a show biz kind of a thing.
Yeah, that's what it was, because he did very well when he had the trio.
Uh-huh.
He was a fine accompanist for himself.
Yeah.
You know?
I think John Collins told me that it was Maria's idea.
Yeah, well it was --
That he should stand up and not play the piano anymore.
For awhile -- I'll tell you how that transition went about. It was the King Cole Trio, and then Nat -- Nat King Cole and the Trio, and then it became Nat King Cole.
Uh-huh.
You know, step to step, stage to stage,
Uh-huh.
And that's the way I think the image went.
And as the sidemen got more anonymous their pay went up, because that was their compensation. Lots of money but we're not going to tell anybody who you are.
Yes. Just go into oblivion.
